case: Eurodrone fictional eco-design and supply resilience

cues.text: In ASRI, we will examine supply chain resilience and eco-design using the Eurodrone case.
We select Create Your Own Strategic Case to evaluate decisions from an operational perspective.
In Investigate, we choose Eurodrone and focus on decisions involving critical materials.
Select Eco-design and Critical Materials. ASRI loads the case definition and three comparable alternatives.
The case definition identifies a support subsystem and the scope of the decision under review.
The question is whether repair and supplier diversification can reduce in-service vulnerabilities.
Before comparing, we set the same component, functional requirement and assessment period.
We continue to Challenge, where operating and economic conditions drive the results.
We compare the current baseline, qualified repair and a combined option with an alternative supplier.
All six sections follow the same structure. Only the applicable parameters differ.
Open Operational Conditions. Each input shows the three options using equivalent units.
Recovery time indicates how long each option takes without additional incidents.
The binding supply lead time reflects the wait for a component or supplier when it affects the decision.
The deadline is shared. ASRI evaluates whether each strategy could meet it given the stated risks.
Open Risks and Probabilities to enter success likelihood and potential disruptions.
We distinguish technical success probability from the delay caused by failure of the chosen route.
We also assess the possibility of an external disruption and the additional days it could cause.
Economic Obligations covers direct costs, logistics and additional commitments under disruption.
Expected cost weights those expenses by probability to compare options within the same boundary.
Contractual Conditions lets us assess reservations and penalties whenever those obligations apply.
If a condition is irrelevant, mark it Not Applicable and record why, rather than inventing a zero.
Environmental Factors covers materials, waste and greenhouse gases within a defined boundary.
These indicators reveal trade-offs between circularity, availability and cost.
The sixth section covers evidence and uncertainty: every input needs an appropriate source and review.
The dashboard compares time, deadline attainment, cost and environmental outcomes without imposing a winner.
We change the recovery time for the repair option to test how the model responds.
The calculation updates immediately, allowing us to examine sensitivity before deciding.
We restore the original value to keep the comparison consistent.
The sensitivity margin shows whether conclusions depend strongly on a particular assumption.
One option may improve one indicator and worsen another. ASRI makes those trade-offs visible.
We move to Check to identify which conclusions are adequately supported.
In Check, we assess data quality and the technical requirements that must be supported.
Four review gates cover comparable scope, technical eligibility, measurement method and independent review.
Every gate requires proper verification. A tick box does not replace formal approval.
The register identifies each document, owner, reviewer, review date and limitations.
We add a reference awaiting review to illustrate how traceability is organised.
Each alternative input can then be linked to a traceable and comparable source.
The review status shows what is still required before a conclusion can be confirmed.
With inputs and evidence clearly framed, we reach Translate: the strategic centre of ASRI.
Translate turns technical findings into value that matters to the person making a decision.
This is the difference: an environmental result is not enough. We must show which vulnerability changes.
The question moves beyond how much material is saved towards which industrial dependencies we can reduce.
Repairability can reduce the need for new procurement; diversification can create additional supply options.
Those mechanisms still require technical feasibility and comparable evidence.
Select Defence Customer. The same comparison is framed in terms of mission continuity.
Can we sustain the required capability if a supplier can no longer deliver a critical component?
The customer's potential value is reduced exposure to disruption without compromising operational requirements.
Now choose Engineering. Value depends on repair and materials meeting technical requirements.
Here we need testing, supplier qualification, traceability and proper approval of changes.
Translate clarifies what Engineering needs to demonstrate before an advantage can be defended.
Select Programme Manager. The message shifts to availability, schedules and commitments.
Material savings have operational value only if they do not create new delays, costs or dependencies.
Here we weigh the trade-offs: how timing changes, what it costs and which risks remain.
Finally, choose Executive Leadership. We turn scattered indicators into a strategic decision.
The question is where investment can strengthen industrial autonomy and response capability.
Translate does not invent benefits; it prioritises risks, options and the evidence needed.
One analysis supports four different decision conversations without changing the underlying facts.
That is how ASRI translates sustainability into the language of resilience our stakeholders expect.
For a Defence customer, the focus is operational continuity and access to critical components.
For Engineering, we focus on qualification, safety and verifiable repairability.
For the Programme team, we relate findings to timing, costs, milestones and supply commitments.
For leadership, we address industrial dependencies, risk exposure and the value of decisions.
We switch the selected option to show how the message changes without altering the method.
Translate retains traceability and clearly identifies what still needs to be verified.
That argument can be included in a report alongside the comparison and supporting evidence.
The PDF report brings together the case, results, evidence and audience-specific interpretation.
A Markdown version is also available for reviewing and editing the content.
Before sharing, ensure the figures are comparable and the conclusion has appropriate support.
We can download an editable case file and continue the analysis whenever needed.
ASRI connects sustainability decisions to the resilience that matters to customers, programmes and leadership.
